text: The Standard-Model paper of the series needs one hypothesis for the lepton doublet, the singlet listing and its unifying group: that the composite's state space is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, three pair modes and two slot modes. This note asks whether the tower derives it. The exact part: the spinor module of the $n$-rung transport $\Cl(2,4) \to \Cl(2{+}n, 4{+}n)$ is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{n})$, so the hypothesis says that a two-twistor composite lives two rungs up; the rung-and-pair mixings are $U(n) \times U(3)$ acting as the hypothesis prescribes; the ladder group of the Standard-Model paper is this $U(n)$ on the one-constituent sector; the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the real form fixed by the tower's adjoint structure once its frames are fixed; and the mass bracket of the mass paper is the frozen point's grip, at $\Lambda = 0$, on the slot-antisymmetric bivector. Given these and the identification of slots with rungs, the rung and slot-statistics hypotheses are one hypothesis in two languages. The part that does not close: no theorem of the series makes each twistor a rung. One completion transports every null momentum at once; the null bivectors of any number of twistors invite one further rung, together, and that rung's $U(2)$ mixes chirality; and the module holds the composite's tuple as one vector, not two twistors. So the hypothesis is sharpened to one structural sentence with a named missing mechanism and, failing that, registered at Tier C with priced kill conditions. Every identity is verified exactly by a deposited script.

title: What we assume

text: \emph{Hypothesis (R), the rung reading.} The internal state space of a composite of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor composite) is the spinor module of the $n$-th rung of the tower above $\Cl(2,4)$, $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{n})$, on which the transported algebra acts as in Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}: each conformal spinor of the composite occupies one new rung, and the constituents are the states with one rung occupied.

title: Imported: the tower, one qubit per rung
text: The transport principle completes $\Cl(p,q)$ to $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ by adjoining one hyperbolic pair, and the completed algebra carries a null cone of its own, so the completion iterates: the $k$-th rung is $T_{k} = \Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k)$, with adjoined null pairs $v_{j}, w_{j}$ satisfying, as vectors, $v_{i}v_{j} + v_{j}v_{i} = 0$, $w_{i}w_{j} + w_{j}w_{i} = 0$ and $v_{i}w_{j} + w_{j}v_{i} = \delta_{ij}$. title: The exact part: what the tower's spinor module is, and how the paper's objects sit in it
The $n$-rung spinor module and its mixings
text:
Let $\Cl(2{+}n, 4{+}n)$ be the $n$-th rung of the tower above $\Cl(2,4)$, with new isotropic directions $v_{1}, \ldots, v_{n}$ spanning $R_{n} \cong \C^{n}$ after complexification. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Its complexified spinor module is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{n}) = \Sp \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{n}$, of dimension $2^{3+n}$, graded by $(j, k)$ with $j$ the number of new modes and $k$ the number of old pairs occupied, and irreducible; its chirality is the parity of $j + k$. At $n = 2$ this is the five-mode ledger of Hypothesis (S), with the same grading and the same chirality rule.
\item The subgroup of unitaries of $W \oplus R_{n}$ preserving the two summands is $U(3) \times U(n)$, and it acts on the module as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(B \oplus A)$: on $\Lambda^{j}R_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ by $\Lambda^{j}(A) \otimes \Lambda^{k}(B)$. At $n = 2$ this is exactly the action Hypothesis (S) prescribes.
\item The Bogoliubov group of the $3 + n$ modes is the compact orthogonal group $O(6{+}2n)$, implemented by $\mathrm{Pin}(6{+}2n)$. At $n = 2$ the connected part is $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, acting irreducibly on each chirality half; the half of even $j + k$ is the sixteen-dimensional half-spin representation, which under (S) is the generation of Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}. The number-preserving subgroup of $\mathrm{Spin}(6{+}2n)$ is a double cover of $U(3{+}n)$, acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet} \otimes \det^{-1/2}$; on the determinant-one subgroup this agrees with the action of (2), and it is the determinant-one part that (S) uses (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). At $n = 3$ the group is $\mathrm{Spin}(12)$, and the split-and-number-preserving $U(3) \times U(3)$, of dimension eighteen, acts faithfully on the module, while its action on the cell sector $\Lambda^{1}R_{3} \otimes \Lambda^{1}W = \C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ has kernel $K = \{(\lambda I_{3}, \lambda^{-1}I_{3})\}$ and image the seventeen of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}: the seventeen is the $n = 3$ cell action, exactly as the twelve of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ is the $n = 2$ cell action of a thirteen-dimensional group on the module. (At $n = 3$ the trace-free subalgebra $\{\tr X + \tr X' = 0\}$ contains $K$'s generator, so the seventeen is the quotient and not that subalgebra, unlike $n = 2$ where $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ maps isomorphically onto the cell action. This clause is a relabelling: the cell sector is $\C^{3} \otimes \C^{3}$ with the group Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton} already has, and nothing about the tower enters.)
\item The dimension counts: $2^{3+n} = 8, 16, 32, 64$ for $n = 0, 1, 2, 3$; $\dim \mathfrak{so}(6{+}2n) = 15, 28, 45, 66$; $\dim(\uu(3) \oplus \uu(n)) = 9, 10, 13, 18$.
\end{enumerate}
proof: (1) By Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}, $T_{n} \cong \Cl(2,4) \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2^{n}}(\R)$, and after complexification $\Cl(2,4) \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$ acting irreducibly on $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}) while $B_{n} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{2^{n}}(\C)$ acts irreducibly on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W_{n} \otimes \C = \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{n}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}); the tensor product $\mathrm{M}_{8} \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2^{n}} = \mathrm{M}_{8 \cdot 2^{n}}$ acts irreducibly on $\Sp \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{n}$, which is the whole endomorphism algebra of that space, so this is the spinor module of $T_{n} \otimes \C$, of dimension $2^{3+n}$. The step from the twisted presentation to the mode grading: the tensor decomposition $A_{n} \otimes B_{n}$ of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} presents $T_{n}$ through the twisted ground generators, which are not vectors of $\R^{2+n,4+n}$; but $T_{n} \otimes \C$ is also generated by the $6 + 2n$ untwisted vectors, so it is the complex Clifford algebra on $6 + 2n$ generators (\claimref{std-algebra.complexification}), $\mathrm{M}_{2^{3+n}}(\C)$, whose irreducible module is unique up to isomorphism and is the Fock module of any $3 + n$ anticommuting mode pairs (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}); the pairs of $W$ with its dual and the untwisted $(v_{j}, w_{j})$ are such a set, and their Fock module is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus R_{n})$ by the direct-sum formula for exterior algebras \cite[App.~B.2]{FultonHarris1991}, with the grading by occupied modes the bigrading $\Lambda^{j}R_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$. The irreducibility established through $A_{n} \otimes B_{n}$ transfers to this presentation because the module is the same up to isomorphism. The chirality of a Fock module is its parity grading (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}), here $(-1)^{j+k}$. At $n = 2$, $R_{2} = \C^{2}$ and the description is (S)'s. (2) A unitary of $W \oplus R_{n}$ preserving the summands is $B \oplus A$, and the induced action on the exterior algebra is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(B \oplus A) = \Lambda^{\bullet}(B) \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(A)$ on $\Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{n}$, degree by degree. (3) is Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group} with $E = W \oplus R_{n}$, $\dim E = 3 + n$, the Hermitian structure being the one under which $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}); the double cover and the $\det^{-1/2}$ twist are the "determinant phase" of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, absent on the determinant-one subgroup. The $n = 3$ clause: $\uu(3) \oplus \uu(3)$ has dimension $18$; $K$'s generator $(iI_{3}, -iI_{3})$ acts on $\Lambda^{j}R_{3} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ by $i(j - k)$, zero exactly on the cells $j = k = 1$ and nonzero on the module, so the action on the module is faithful and the action on the cells has kernel $K$; the quotient, of dimension $17$, is the seventeen of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}; and the trace-free subalgebra, which contains the kernel since $\tr(iI_{3}) + \tr(-iI_{3}) = 0$, acts on the cells with rank $16$ only. The script confirms the ranks $17$ and $16$ at $n = 3$ against $12$ and $12$ at $n = 2$, and the eigenvalue $j - k$. (4) is arithmetic, script-checked.

title: The compact form
text: The ambient signature at rung two is $(4,6)$, whose spin group is the noncompact $\mathrm{Spin}(4,6)$; the group in Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3) is the compact $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. They are two real forms of one complex group sharing the module, and the compact one is the real form fixed by the $*$-structure of the tower (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), under which the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_{j}^{*} = w_{j}$: that adjointness is the Hermitian structure of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, and the Bogoliubov group preserving it is the compact one. The $*$-structure is defined once the tower's frames are fixed, as T3 fixes them, so "fixed by" means fixed given the frames, a choice of maximal compact subgroup made once for the whole series rather than a consequence of the relations alone. The pattern is already present one rung down, where the ambient real form is the conformal $SU(2,2) \cong \mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}) while the pair-mixing group is the unitary group $U(3)$ of $W$ for the same adjointness, inside the compact three-mode Bogoliubov group. A grand-unification group must be compact, and the tower supplies the compact form for the same reason it supplies $U(3)$.

title: The mass bracket is the frozen point's grip on the slot-antisymmetric bivector, at $\Lambda = 0$
text:
In the chart $\CS = \Som \oplus \Spi$ of the conformal spinor space (twistor space), the $E = -1$ and $E = +1$ eigenspaces, with bases $e_{1}, e_{2}$ of $\Som$ and $\pi_{1}, \pi_{2}$ of $\Spi$, normalise $\varepsilon(e_{1} \wedge e_{2} \wedge \pi_{1} \wedge \pi_{2}) = 1$ and let $n_{\infty} = e_{1} \wedge e_{2} \in \Lambda^{2}\Som \subset \Lambda^{2}\CS \cong V_{\C}$, the bivector of the line at infinity. For conformal spinors $Z^{i} = (\omega^{i}, \pi^{i})$,
\[
\varepsilon\bigl(n_{\infty} \wedge Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2}\bigr) \;=\; \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
m^{2} \;=\; 2\,\bigl|\varepsilon(n_{\infty} \wedge Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2})\bigr|^{2}
\]
by Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}; and $\varepsilon(n_{0} \wedge Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2}) = \br{\omega^{1}\omega^{2}}$ for $n_{0} = \pi_{1} \wedge \pi_{2}$, so that the frozen point at general $\Lambda$ pairs to $\varepsilon(I_{\Lambda} \wedge Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} + (\Lambda/6)\br{\omega^{1}\omega^{2}}$, the $\Lambda = 0$ term being the mass bracket. In the language of the $n$-tuple $\Psi = \sum_{i} e_{i}' \otimes Z^{i} \in \C^{2} \otimes \CS$ (with $e_{i}'$ the slot basis, over the complex unit $I_{6}$), the total momentum is the slot trace of $\Psi \otimes \bar\Psi$ restricted to the $\pi$-parts, and $Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2}$ is the $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{2}\CS$ component of $\Psi \odot \Psi$: at $\Lambda = 0$ the mass is the frozen point's pairing with the slot-antisymmetric bivector, and vanishes exactly when that bivector is orthogonal to the frozen point.
proof: Expand $Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2} = \omega^{1}\wedge\omega^{2} + (\omega^{1}\wedge\pi^{2} - \omega^{2}\wedge\pi^{1}) + \pi^{1}\wedge\pi^{2}$. Wedging with $e_{1} \wedge e_{2}$ kills every term with an $\omega$ factor, leaving $e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge\pi^{1}\wedge\pi^{2} = \det(\pi^{i}_{A})\,e_{1}\wedge e_{2}\wedge\pi_{1}\wedge\pi_{2}$, and $\det(\pi^{i}_{A}) = \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}$; the $n_{0}$ case is the same with the roles exchanged. That $n_{\infty}$ is the bivector of $\Som$ and is the frozen point at $\Lambda = 0$ is Facts \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line} and \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}. For the tuple: $\Psi \otimes \bar\Psi = \sum_{ij} e_{i}' \otimes \bar e_{j}' \otimes Z^{i} \otimes \bar Z^{j}$, and contracting the slot indices with $\delta_{ij}$ gives $\sum_{i} Z^{i} \otimes \bar Z^{i}$, whose $\pi \otimes \bar\pi$ part is $p$; and $S^{2}(\C^{2} \otimes \CS) = S^{2}\C^{2} \otimes S^{2}\CS \oplus \Lambda^{2}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{2}\CS$, the second summand of $\Psi \odot \Psi$ being $(e_{1}' \wedge e_{2}') \otimes (Z^{1} \wedge Z^{2})$. The script checks the two volume identities on rational instances.

title: The ladder group is the rung-mixing group on the one-constituent sector
text: The $U(n)$ of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton} acts on the $n$-tuple $\Psi \in \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ of conformal spinors (twistors), $\CS$ the conformal spinor space, as $U \otimes 1$. Under Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) the rung-mixing $U(n)$ acts on the sector $\Lambda^{1}R_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W = \C^{n} \otimes \CS$ as $A \otimes 1$. The two actions coincide: the ladder of the Standard-Model paper is the mixing of the new rungs of the tower, restricted to the states with exactly one new mode occupied and an even number of old pairs. The same holds for the pair-mixing $U(3)$, which acts on $\CS$ by $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(B)$ in both.
proof: Both are $A \otimes 1$ on $\C^{n} \otimes \CS$ by construction, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton} for the first and Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) at $j = 1$, $k$ even, for the second; the identification $\Lambda^{1}R_{n} = \C^{n}$ sends the slot basis to the new modes $v_{1}, \ldots, v_{n}$. The $U(3)$ statement is Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) at $j = 1$ read on the $W$ factor. The proposition is definitional once the slot basis is identified with the rung basis; its content is that this identification is available, not that it is forced, and the script computes the rung operators of $\uu(2)$ on the sector and finds the ladder action and nothing leaving the sector.

title: What this identifies, and what it does not
text: Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one} is exact, and it is the one place where the tower and the Standard-Model paper's objects are literally the same thing: the ladder's $U(n)$, derived from momentum and helicity preservation, and the tower's rung-mixing group, derived from the completion, agree on $\C^{n} \otimes \CS$, $\CS$ the conformal spinor space (twistor space). But the identification is on that sector only. The ladder theorem says nothing about the other sectors ($j \neq 1$, or $k$ odd), and the tower says nothing about momentum. To say that the composite's state space is the whole module is a hypothesis, stated next.

title: The exact part: what the tower's spinor module is, and how the paper's objects sit in it
(R) and (S) are one hypothesis in two languages
text: Given Facts \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} and \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, Hypothesis (R) at $n = 2$ implies Hypothesis (S); and (S), together with the identification of the two slots with the two rungs, implies (R) at $n = 2$. At $n = 2$ that identification is a relabelling of two basis vectors, so (R) and (S) are equivalent up to it. Under either, the constituent hypothesis of T12's successor problem (6), a slot vector times a Dirac state with the slot mixing acting once, holds as the $j = 1$ sector; the derived generation is the even half of the module (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); the mass bracket is the pairing of Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}; and $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is the Bogoliubov group of the composite's modes.
proof: (R) $\Rightarrow$ (S): by Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(1) and (2) the module of (R) is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$ with the $(j,k)$ grading, the action $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ of the rung-and-pair mixing group and chirality $(-1)^{j+k}$. (S) speaks of the automorphism group of the hierarchy (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}) acting by $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ (the $U(n)$ action on the Fock space of \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}); the two groups are identified on the one-constituent sector by Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one}, and (R)'s clause that each conformal spinor occupies one rung extends the identification of slots with rungs, hence of the hierarchy's $U(2) \times U(3)$ with the rung-and-pair mixing group, to the whole module. With that identification the module, grading, action and chirality are (S) clause by clause. (S) $\Rightarrow$ (R): (S)'s space is $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$, which by Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(1) is the two-rung module, and (S)'s action is the rung-and-pair mixing of Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2); the transported algebra's action is the Chevalley action on the exterior algebra (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), which (S)'s space carries, so (R) holds once slots are identified with rungs, which is the identification the statement names. The remaining clauses are Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}, and Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3). The proposition is a relabelling made exact, and is stated as a proposition rather than a theorem for that reason: its content is that the two hypotheses have the same module, grading, group action and chirality, so that nothing is gained or lost in passing between them, and that the passage adds exactly one identification, slots with rungs.

title: The generators outside the gauge algebra
text: Under (R) or (S), of the forty-five generators of $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ acting on the composite's modes, exactly thirteen preserve the slot-pair split and the mode number, spanning $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$; exactly twenty-five preserve the mode number, spanning $\uu(5)$; so thirty-two lie outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$, twelve of them inside $\uu(5)$, moving one excitation between a rung and a pair, and twenty changing the mode number by two.
proof: Here the imaginary unit is $I_{4}$, which commutes with every mode operator. The Majorana generators $\gamma_{2i} = a_{i} + a_{i}^{\dagger}$, $\gamma_{2i+1} = I_{4}(a_{i} - a_{i}^{\dagger})$ of the five modes (by \claimref{rungs.hyp-r-rung-reading} or \claimref{standard-model.hyp-s-slot-statistics}) satisfy the Clifford relations, and the forty-five bilinears $\gamma_{p}\gamma_{q}$, $p < q$, span $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}). The bilinears from one mode, $\gamma_{2i}\gamma_{2i+1} = I_{4}(2a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{i} - 1)$, five of them, and from two modes $i \neq j$ the two combinations $a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j} - a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i}$ and $I_{4}(a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j} + a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i})$, twenty of them, commute with the total number operator and span $\uu(5)$, of dimension twenty-five; the remaining two combinations from each pair of modes, $a_{i}a_{j} \pm a_{i}^{\dagger}a_{j}^{\dagger}$ up to factors of $I_{4}$, twenty of them, change the mode number by two. Of the twenty-five, those with $i, j$ both rungs or both pairs commute with the rung and pair numbers separately: $5 + 2 + 6 = 13$, spanning $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$; the other twelve, with one rung index and one pair index, move an excitation across the split. The script computes the two centralisers as exact kernels, of dimensions $25$ and $13$, and exhibits the spanning sets.

title: The part that does not close: no mechanism makes a twistor a rung
The part that does not close: no mechanism makes a twistor a rung
text: Proposition \claimref{rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two} replaces one hypothesis by another of the same strength, and the gain is only that (R) is a sentence about the tower, an object the series has theorems about, rather than a sentence about slot statistics, which it does not. A derivation of (R) would need a mechanism producing one rung per twistor. Three candidates present themselves, and none works as stated.

title: Null momenta invite one rung, together
text: Let $p^{1}, \ldots, p^{n}$ be null vectors of $\R^{1,3} \subset \Cl(1,3)$, the momenta of $n$ massless conformal spinors (twistors). No extension of $\Cl(1,3)$ carries a $\mathrm{Spin}^{0}$-equivariant element-level inverse of the null vectors, so none inverts the $p^{i}$ in the sense the transport principle asks; the minimal completion that the transport principle prescribes is the single rung $\Cl(2,4)$, unique up to isometry and independent of $n$; and on that completion's quadric the transported reciprocal is total, sending every $p^{i}$ to its ideal point $[p^{i} + \tfrac12 n_{\infty}]$ at once. The transport principle completes the quadratic space, not each zero divisor: a second null momentum invites no second rung.
proof: All three clauses are Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} applied to $(\R^{1,3}, \eta)$, which is nondegenerate of mixed signature: the no-go for element-level inverses, the minimality and uniqueness of the one-plane completion, and the totality of the reciprocal on the quadric. The rung is determined by the quadratic space alone, whose null cone contains every $p^{i}$, and the reciprocal's totality is a statement about all null vectors of that cone simultaneously. A second conformal spinor changes the configuration, not the quadratic space. The corollary adds nothing to Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} beyond the observation that its hypotheses concern the quadratic space and not the number of null vectors named. The script confirms, in the blade engine, that a null $p$ stays null in $\Cl(2,4)$ and in $\Cl(3,5)$ (the rung is an isometric extension and inverts nothing as an element) and that the rungs supply one further anticommuting null pair each, orthogonal to $p$.

title: The bivector of two conformal spinors is null, invites one rung, and that rung's $U(2)$ mixes chirality
text: For conformal spinors (twistors) $Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n} \in \CS$, where $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$ is the conformal spinor space with complex unit $I_6$ (not the Dirac module $\Sp = \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ below), every pairwise bivector $Z^{i} \wedge Z^{j} \in \Lambda^{2}\CS \cong V_{\C}$ is a null vector of the complexified ambient space of $\Cl(2,4)$, decomposable by construction, and for $n = 2$, $m^{2} = 2|\varepsilon(n_{\infty} \wedge Z^{1}\wedge Z^{2})|^{2}$ by Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}. The transport principle iterates on the real ambient space $\R^{2,4}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), and Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} applied to it gives one further hyperbolic plane, unique, with a reciprocal total on the whole real cone, whatever $n$: the mechanism is a completion of one quadratic space and depends on no count of conformal spinors. The one-rung module $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C v)$, of dimension sixteen, is $\C^{2} \otimes \Sp$ as a vector space, the constituent space of (C), and the transported algebra does supply a $U(2)$ on the $\C^{2}$ factor: the unitary group of the rung's own Clifford algebra $B_{1} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$, the commutant of the ground algebra. But that $U(2)$ contains the odd elements $v \pm w$ of the rung, which anticommute with the chirality operator; its chirality-preserving part is the abelian $\{1, vw\}$-span, a torus. So one rung gives (C)'s vector space with a $U(2)$ that mixes the chirality of the two constituent states, while (C), (S) and the ladder need a $U(2)$ acting within one chirality, which is the rung-mixing $U(2)$ on $\Lambda^{1}R_{2}$ of Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2), available at two rungs.
proof: Decomposability is the form of $Z^{i} \wedge Z^{j}$; nullity of decomposable bivectors is Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}; the mass identity is Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}. Whether a given complex null bivector lies on the real cone is the nullity of its line for the reversion form $\Sigma$, the twistor form (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}), which a massive pair need not satisfy; the argument does not need it, since it is the real quadratic space $\R^{2,4}$ that is completed, and $\R^{2,4}$ is nondegenerate of mixed signature, so Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion} applies to it exactly as to $\R^{1,3}$ in Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}. One rung above $\Cl(2,4)$ has module $\Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C v) = \Sp \otimes \C^{2}$ and $T_{1} \cong A_{1} \otimes B_{1}$ with $B_{1} \cong \Cl(1,1) \cong \mathrm{M}_{2}(\R)$ acting irreducibly on the qubit and commuting with the twisted ground algebra $A_{1}$ (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}); after complexification $A_{1} \otimes \C \cong \mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$, so the commutant of $A_{1}$ in $\mathrm{End}(\Sp \otimes \C^{2}) = \mathrm{M}_{8} \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2}$ is $1 \otimes \mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$, whose unitary group is $U(2)$. The rung's vectors $v, w$ are odd for the mode-number grading, so they anticommute with $(-1)^{N}$, and the even part of $\mathrm{M}_{2}(\C)$ is spanned by $1$ and $vw$, which commute. At two rungs the new modes span $\C^{2}$ and $U(2) \subset U(5)$ acts on $\Lambda^{1}R_{2} = \C^{2}$ within a fixed chirality (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2)). The script checks the nullity of all six pairwise bivectors of an instance with four conformal spinors, and, on the four-mode Fock space, that the twisted ground generators generate $\mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$, that the rung's $\{1, v, w, vw\}$ commutes with them, that $v$ and $w$ anticommute with chirality, and that the even part is abelian.

title: The transported module holds the tuple as one vector, not as two conformal spinors
text: The configuration space of two conformal spinors (two twistors) of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}, as a vector space, is $\CS \oplus \CS = \C^{2} \otimes \CS$, $\CS$ the conformal spinor space, eight-dimensional, carrying the continuous data $(\omega^{i}, \pi^{i})$, the parts of each spinor in the $E = -1$ and $E = +1$ eigenspaces at the origin; it is the sector $(j, k) \in \{(1,0), (1,2)\}$ of the two-rung module, which under $U(2) \times U(3)$ is, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, $(2,1)_{1/2} \oplus (2,\bar{3})_{-1/6}$, the antiparticle doublets $L^{*} \oplus Q^{*}$ in the orientation of T12's listing or $L \oplus Q$ in the opposite one. The two-particle tensor product $\CS \otimes \CS$, by contrast, has no $U(3)$-equivariant embedding in the module: it contains $S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$, the six-dimensional $SU(3)$-irreducible $\bar{6}$, while every sector of the module is a multiple of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, whose $SU(3)$ content is $1, 3, \bar{3}, 1$. And the mass bracket, the $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{2}\CS$ component of $\Psi \odot \Psi$ (Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}), is quadratic in $\Psi$ and lives in $S^{2}$ of the module, not in the module. So the module treats the composite as T12 does, as one tuple $\Psi$ with a slot index, and not as a product state of two conformal spinors.
proof: The sector statement is Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) at $j = 1$, $k \in \{0, 2\}$, with the weights $3 - 2k = 3, -1$ of Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, and $\Lambda^{1}R_{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W = \C^{2} \otimes \CS$ as in Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one}. The $\bar{6}$: $\Lambda^{2}W \otimes \Lambda^{2}W = S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W) \oplus \Lambda^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$, and $S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$ has the weight $2(e_{1} + e_{2})$, whose class modulo $(1,1,1)$ is not a weight of $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, all of whose weights have coordinates in $\{0, 1\}$; so $S^{2}(\Lambda^{2}W)$, irreducible under $SU(3)$ \cite[\S 15.3]{FultonHarris1991}, has no equivariant image in $\Lambda^{\bullet}W \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}R_{2}$, on which $SU(3)$ acts through $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$ alone, and an equivariant map from $\CS \otimes \CS$ must kill it, so is not an embedding. The bracket clause is Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot}. The script checks the weights, the Casimirs of the sectors, and the absent $\bar{6}$ weights.

title: Where this leaves (R)
text: Three things are now exact that were not. The five-mode ledger is the tower's two-rung module, so (S) is a statement about the tower. The ladder group is the rung-mixing group on the one-constituent sector. And the mass bracket is the frozen point's grip on the slot-antisymmetric bivector, at $\Lambda = 0$, which is a null vector of the ambient space that invites the next rung. What is missing is a single mechanism: why a conformal spinor constituent (a twistor) occupies a rung. The count is the obstacle. Null momenta invite one rung in total (Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}); the bivectors of two conformal spinors invite one more, together (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}); neither gives one rung per constituent, and the second gives the right vector space with a $U(2)$ that mixes chirality. The precise form of the missing statement is this: the composite's internal algebra is generated by $3 + n$ anticommuting mode pairs, the three pairs of $W$ shared and one new pair per constituent. Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung} then supplies everything else, the module, the grading and the groups. Why a conformal spinor constituent should contribute exactly one mode to the composite, rather than none (the tensor ledger of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}, where the slots are labels and the pairs are shared) or three (a copy of $W$ per constituent, the product state that Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector} excludes), is the question, and the note has no argument for it. It belongs to the tower paper, where the mode count is a theorem about the real Witt index and where a statement about what a conformal spinor constituent contributes to a composite's algebra would have to be made.

title: The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise
The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise
text:
If the missing statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.where-leaves-r} is not supplied, the series' own rule for a structural premise that resists derivation is to register it at Tier C, with its predictions and its kill conditions priced. The registration, in the form T12 uses for its stances:

\begin{quote}
\emph{Registered premise (S), equivalently (R).} The internal state space of the minimal massive composite is the five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(W \oplus \C^{2})$, the two-rung transport of the twistor completion, with the gauge group below the intermediate scale acting through Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2) on its determinant-one part (the thirteenth generator, anomaly-free in the action the state space carries, being broken at that scale, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}) and chirality the parity of the mode number.
\end{quote}

\noindent\emph{What it predicts.} (i) Exactly one generation per composite, the sixteen of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$: quark and lepton doublets, four singlets, the fourth at hypercharge zero (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); that the composite carries no further chiral state is the registration's own reading of "the state space is this Fock space", not a clause of Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}. (ii) The $\mathbb{Z}_{6}$ charge lattice of T12 Theorem 4.2; this is unconditional in T12 and is not a test of (S), and is listed because (S) must respect it and does (Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}). (iii) Unification into $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ with $\sin^{2}\theta_{W} = 3/8$ at the unification scale, hence, with the desert dead (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}), a change in the running between the weak and unification scales: partner-like content, or an intermediate symmetry such as T12's Pati-Salam route, on which $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ is an input. (iv) Baryon and lepton number violation by the thirty-two generators of $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ outside $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ (Proposition \claimref{rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra}): twelve that move an excitation between a rung and a pair (the leptoquark directions of $\uu(5)$), and twenty that create or annihilate two modes at once.

\noindent\emph{What kills it.} (a) A confirmed chiral fermion outside the sixteen per generation, or a fourth colour singlet with nonzero hypercharge (the anomaly conditions would then admit a family, Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). (b) A fractionally charged colour singlet, off the lattice; this kills the exclusion stance of T12 Theorem 4.2 whether or not (S) holds, so it is a kill shared with T12, not one that discriminates (S). (c) A measured $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}$ at a scale where the three couplings can be shown, with the observed spectrum plus any partner content compatible with the sixteen, not to meet: the two-loop run with thresholds, T12 successor problem (2). (d) A proton lifetime bound incompatible with any $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ breaking scale allowed by (iii); the framework does not yet fix that scale, so this condition is priced as inherited from the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ literature rather than sharpened. (e) Internally: a proof that the composite's internal algebra closes on the three pair modes alone, with the slots as labels (the tensor ledger reading of Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}), which would refute (R) directly and leave (S) without its only structural reading.

\noindent\emph{Level.} A structural premise with priced kill conditions is Tier C by the series' definition; T12 is declared Tier B, and if (S) is registered rather than derived the sections that rest on it (T12 Proposition 5.3(2), Theorem 5.5(1), the consistency clause of (3), the last clause of Proposition 5.6, Proposition 5.8, Remark 5.9, and Proposition 6.1's values $3/8$ and $3/4$, which are taken over a generation containing the lepton; without the lepton the ratio is $9/26$) carry Tier C and the abstract should say so. The sections that do not rest on it, the algebra, the global form, the converse, the quark doublet, the singlet spectrum as a computation on the single-twistor Fock space, the uniqueness arithmetic given a charge list, the trace ratios as arithmetic over any tabulated content with $9/10$ over the fibre, and the run, stay at Tier B.

title: Position in the series
Position in the series
text: This note is a companion to T12 of the series, alongside a companion note on the lepton, which asks whether the lepton is derivable inside the two-level hierarchy and answers no. \emph{It relies on:} the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} for the rungs, the Fock module and the Witt index (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}), and the transport principle paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the totality and minimality of the completion (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-totality-minimality-completion}); the twistor paper T9 \cite{ButlerT9} for the spinor identification, the Witt data and the line at infinity (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-spinor-identification-witt-data-line}); the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} for the two-twistor mass formula (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-mass-symplectic-area}); and the Standard-Model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the ladder, the automorphism group, Hypothesis (S), the derived generation, the constituent hypothesis of its successor problem (6), and the results priced in the section ``The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise'' (Facts \claimref{rungs.imported-ladder-automorphism-group-no-lepton}, \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}, \claimref{rungs.imported-results-t12-used-registration}). \emph{Papers that would rely on it:} T12, if (R) replaces (S) as the premise or is derived; the tower paper T3, if the missing statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.where-leaves-r} is taken up there, where it belongs; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17}, which would record (S) as a registered premise with the kill conditions of the section ``The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise''.

title: Machine verification
Machine verification
text: Every computational identity asserted here is verified in exact arithmetic by the deposited script \cite{ButlerVerifyT12R}, \texttt{verify\_T12\_rungs.py}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py}: seventeen checks, all passing, no floating point (ranks are computed by \texttt{GA.py}'s elimination over exact rationals). The script builds the five-mode Fock representation explicitly, as thirty-two by thirty-two matrices over the Gaussian integers, and the four-mode one of a single rung, and computes on them rather than restating formulas. They are: the canonical anticommutation relations, the uniqueness of the vacuum and the spanning of the module by creation monomials (Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}, Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(1)); the chirality operator $(-1)^{N}$ as the parity of $j + k$, anticommuting with every generator; the bigraded dimensions counted on the basis; the ten Majorana generators' Clifford relations and the linear independence of the forty-five bilinears; their closure under the commutator with the $\mathfrak{so}(10)$ bracket on all pairs, and their commuting with chirality (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the exact dimensions $25$ and $13$ of the subalgebras commuting with the total and with the separate mode numbers, giving $45 - 13 = 32 = 12 + 20$ (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(2), (3), Proposition \claimref{rungs.generators-outside-gauge-algebra}, the section ``The fallback: (S) as a Tier C premise''(iv)); the selection of $3N_{\mathrm{rung}} - 2N_{\mathrm{pair}}$ as the trace-free element of the centre, with eigenvalue $3j - 2k$, and the eigenvalue $j - k$ of $K$'s generator, zero on the cells only (Proposition \claimref{rungs.r-s-are-one-hypothesis-two}, Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the $\su(2)$ and $\su(3)$ Casimirs on every sector and the weights of $\Lambda^{2}W$ (Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector}, Fact \claimref{standard-model.under-s-composites-state-space-spinor}); the ranks $17$ and $16$ at $n = 3$ against $12$ and $12$ at $n = 2$ (Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(3)); the two volume identities of Lemma \claimref{rungs.mass-bracket-frozen-points-grip-slot} on rational instances and the partial trace of $\Psi \otimes \bar\Psi$ over the slot index on a Gaussian-rational instance; the rung operators of $\uu(2)$ on the one-constituent even sector as the ladder action (Proposition \claimref{rungs.ladder-group-rung-mixing-group-one}); a null momentum staying null in $\Cl(2,4)$ and $\Cl(3,5)$ with the rungs' null pairs in \texttt{GA.py}'s blade engine (Corollary \claimref{rungs.fact-null-momenta-invite-one-rung}); the nullity of all six pairwise bivectors of a four-twistor instance, and, on the four-mode space, the twisted ground generators generating $\mathrm{M}_{8}(\C)$ with the rung's $\{1, v, w, vw\}$ as commutant, $v, w$ anticommuting with chirality and the even part abelian (Proposition \claimref{rungs.two-twistor-bivector-null-invites-one}; the script's twisted generators square to $-1$, so this verifies the complexified statement, not Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-tower-one-qubit-per-rung}'s real isomorphism); the absent $\bar{6}$ weights (Proposition \claimref{rungs.transported-module-holds-tuple-one-vector}); and the dimension counts of Theorem \claimref{rungs.rung-spinor-module-mixings}(4). What the script does not check: the Facts beyond the instances named, verified in their own papers' scripts; the real-form statement of Remark \claimref{note.rungs.compact-form}, which is representation theory imported through Fact \claimref{rungs.imported-fock-representation-bogoliubov-group}; and Hypothesis (R), which is not a computation.

The Fock model of the complexified ascended algebra
text:
Let $W \subset V_\C$ be a maximal totally isotropic subspace ($\dim_\C W = 3$) and $W'$ a complementary maximal isotropic subspace, dual to $W$ under the $\C$-bilinear form (such a pair exists, and any two such pairs are conjugate under $O(V_\C)$). On the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W$ ($\dim_\C = 2^3 = 8$) define
\[
c(w) := \sqrt2\; w \wedge (\cdot) \quad (w \in W),
\qquad
c(w') := \sqrt2\; \iota_{w'} \quad (w' \in W'),
\]
with $\iota$ contraction through the pairing. Then $c(u)^2 = Q(u)\,\id$ for every $u \in W \oplus W' = V_\C$, so $c$ extends to an algebra map $\Cl(V_\C) \to \End(\Lambda^\bullet W)$; this map is an isomorphism, and $\Lambda^\bullet W$ is the unique irreducible module of $\Cl(2,4)_\C$: the Dirac spinors of the completion. Vectors act oddly, so the even and odd halves
\[
\CS := \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} W, \qquad \CSm := \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}} W,
\]
each of complex dimension 4, are modules of the even subalgebra $\Cl^0(2,4)_\C \cong \End(\CS) \oplus \End(\CSm)$: the two chiralities, the conformal spinor space $\CS$ and its opposite $\CSm$ (twistor and dual twistor space).

title: The incidence relation is the chart
text:
Fix bases $\pi_1, \pi_2$ of $\Spi$ and $e_1, e_2$ of $\Som$ with $\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 = N_0$ and $e_1 \wedge e_2 = N_\infty$. For a linear map $A: \Spi \to \Som$ let $L_A := \{A\pi + \pi : \pi \in \Spi\}$ be its graph line and
\[
P(A) \;:=\; (A\pi_1 + \pi_1)\wedge(A\pi_2 + \pi_2) \;\in\; \Lambda^2\CS
\]
its Pl\"ucker bivector, normalised by $P(0) = N_0$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Expansion.)} $P(A) = N_0 + \varphi(A) + (\det A)\, N_\infty$, where $\varphi(A) := A\pi_1\wedge\pi_2 + \pi_1\wedge A\pi_2$ lies in the mixed slot $\Som\wedge\Spi$ and $\det$ is taken in the chosen bases.
\item \emph{(The chart, term by term.)} $\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism onto the mixed slot $= \{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp \otimes \C$, and satisfies $Q(\varphi(A)) = -2\det A$. Writing $m(A) := \varphi(A)$ as a vector of $\{\nO,\nInf\}^\perp\otimes\C$, the Pl\"ucker bivector is exactly the completion's point embedding, complexified:
\[
P(A) \;=\; \nO \,+\, m(A)\,-\,\tfrac12\,Q(m(A))\,\nInf \;=\; X\bigl(m(A)\bigr).
\]
In particular every $P(A)$ is null, as a Pl\"ucker bivector must be, and the nullity of $P(A)$ is equivalent to the identity $\det A = -\tfrac12Q(m(A))$: the quadratic term of the chart is a determinant.
\item \emph{(Coverage.)} $A \mapsto L_A$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ onto the lines of $\PCS$ skew to $L_\infty$, and $[P(A)]$ ranges exactly over the points of the Klein quadric with $\ip{P}{\nInf} \neq 0$: the affine chart of the complexified conformal compactification, with the lines meeting $L_\infty$ as the points at infinity; the real locus is cut out in Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}(5).
\item \emph{(Consequences.)} (i) The null pair adjoined by the Witt completion is the pair of skew lines $(L_\infty, L_0)$ (Proposition \claimref{correspondence.skew-lines-splittings-hyperbolic-planes-one}). (ii) The splitting of a conformal spinor (a twistor) into its $(\omega, \pi)$ parts along $\CS = \Som\oplus\Spi$ is the Witt completion seen at spinor level: the same datum in a third language. (iii) The incidence relation (Penrose's $\omega = ix\pi$; in the real algebra $\omega = \tfrac12 x\,\nInf\,\pi$, real-linear in $x$) is the case $A = I_6\hat x$ of the chart map, with $I_6$ the complex unit of $\CS$ (a factor of $i$: with $I_6 = e_0e_1e_2e_3e_4e_5$, $I_6$ acts as $-i$ on $\CS$) and $\hat x$ Hermitian for the invariant Hermitian form $\Sigma$ (the twistor form) of Proposition \claimref{correspondence.reality-conjugation-twistor-form-factor}(5)). (iv) The stabiliser of the infinity line $L_\infty$ in $\mathfrak{so}(V_\C)$ is the stabiliser of the ray of $\nInf$: the Poincar\'e parabolic, with its Levi factor acting on $\Som \oplus \Spi$ as the two chiral $2$-dimensional representations, one plane the doublet of each $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\C)$ factor of the complexified Lorentz algebra and trivial for the other (Lemma \claimref{correspondence.chiral-planes-summand-spaces}(1)).
\end{enumerate}

title: Reality: the conjugation, the invariant Hermitian form, and the factor $I_6$
text:
Write $v \mapsto \bar v$ for the real structure of $V_\C$ with real points $V$, and $J$ for the antilinear map on $\Lambda^\bullet W$ that conjugates coefficients in the monomial basis built on the isotropic basis of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.fock-model-complexified-ascended-algebra}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{The conjugation.}) With $\Gamma$ the parity operator ($+1$ on $\CS$, $-1$ on $\CSm$) and $b_4$ the fourth negative basis vector of the section ``Setting and imports'',
\[
\kappa := \Gamma\, c(b_4)\, J
\]
is an antilinear bijection of $\Lambda^\bullet W$ with $\kappa\, c(v) = c(\bar v)\, \kappa$ for all $v \in V_\C$; every antilinear map with this property is a complex multiple of $\kappa$; $\kappa$ swaps the chiralities, $\kappa(\CS) = \CSm$; and $\kappa^2 = -\id$.
\item (\emph{The invariant Hermitian form.}) $\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2) := B(\kappa Z_1, Z_2)$ (the twistor form; on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ it corresponds to the reversion form) is a nondegenerate sesquilinear form on $\CS$ with $\Sigma(Z_2, Z_1) = \lambda\,\overline{\Sigma(Z_1, Z_2)}$ for a constant $\lambda$ of modulus one, so that a rescaling of $\kappa$ by a phase makes $\Sigma$ Hermitian; for the $\kappa$ of (1), $\lambda = 1$ and $\Sigma$ is Hermitian as it stands. The real bivectors act $\Sigma$-anti-Hermitianly, so $\Sigma$ is $\mathrm{Spin}(2,4)$-invariant.
\item (\emph{Null planes.}) For every real null vector $v$ the plane of $\Psi(v)$ is $\Sigma$-null. In particular $\Som$ and $\Spi$ are $\Sigma$-null.
\item (\emph{Signature.}) $\Sigma$ has signature $(2,2)$.
\item (\emph{Reality of the chart, and the factor $I_6$.}) The conformal pseudoscalar $I_6$ acts on $\CS$ as its complex unit (the factor $i$). Let $\sigma(\omega, \pi) := \Sigma(\omega, \pi)$ be the resulting perfect pairing $\Som\times\Spi \to \C$, and call $\hat x: \Spi\to\Som$ \emph{$\sigma$-Hermitian} if $\sigma(\hat x\pi, \pi') = \overline{\sigma(\hat x\pi', \pi)}$ for all $\pi, \pi' \in \Spi$. For $A \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Spi, \Som)$ the following are equivalent: (a) the chart point $m(A)$ of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart} is real, $m(A) \in W_{1,3}$; (b) the line $L_A$ is $\Sigma$-null; (c) $A = I_6\hat x$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian. Consequently the real points of the affine chart are exactly the $\Sigma$-null lines skew to $L_\infty$, the incidence relation of a real point reads $\omega = I_6\hat x\pi$ with $\hat x$ $\sigma$-Hermitian, and on real points the chart norm is $Q(m) = -2\det A = 2\det\hat x$ in the bases of Theorem \claimref{correspondence.incidence-relation-chart}.
\end{enumerate}

title: The de Sitter scale and its frozen point
text:
Let $\eta$ be the fixed product of flat spacetime, the chart of Fact \claimref{mass.imported-flat-model-twistor-chart-infinity}, $Q(x) = \eta(x,x)$, and $\sigma(x) := 1 - \Lambda Q(x)/12$; on the region $\sigma \neq 0$ let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be the gravitational field with $\hb(a) = \sigma\,a$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), whose derived metric is $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$. Write tractors in the flat scale as the vectors $\sigma\,n_{\infty} + \mu + \rho\,n_{0}$ of $\Cl(2,4)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The scale tractor of $\sigma$ in the flat scale is
\[
I_{\sigma} = \bigl(\sigma,\; \nabla\sigma,\; -\tfrac14\Box\sigma\bigr) = \Bigl(1 - \frac{\Lambda Q}{12},\; -\frac{\Lambda}{6}\,x_{a},\; \frac{\Lambda}{6}\Bigr),
\]
it is parallel for the connection \claimref{mass.imported-frozen-point-tractor-connection} of $\eta$, and $\ip{I_{\sigma}}{I_{\sigma}} = \Lambda/3$ identically. Hence the derived metric $g = \sigma^{-2}\eta$ is Einstein with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, on the region $\sigma \neq 0$: the gravitational field $\hb = \sigma$ is de Sitter space on flat spacetime, and $I_{\sigma}$ is its frozen point.
\item The constant ambient vector whose scale function is $\sigma$ is
\[
I_{\Lambda} := n_{\infty} + \frac{\Lambda}{6}\, n_{0},
\]
and it is the only one: $\ip{X(x)}{n_{\infty} + \lambda n_{0}} = 1 - \lambda Q(x)/2$, which equals $\sigma$ iff $\lambda = \Lambda/6$, and the points $X(x)$ span the ambient space. The vector $n_{0} + \lambda n_{\infty}$, of the same norm, has scale function $\lambda - Q/2$: the inverted chart, not this one.
\item $\ip{I_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = 2 \cdot \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\ip{n_{\infty}}{n_{0}} = \Lambda/3$, in agreement with (1). At $\Lambda = 0$, $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty}$: the frozen point of flat space is the point at infinity $n_{\infty}$ of the conformal model (the infinity twistor), and, read through the Klein correspondence as a bivector, it becomes non-simple exactly when $\Lambda \neq 0$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Hypothesis (S): slot statistics, derived from the slot-module hypothesis
text:
\emph{Hypothesis (S), slot statistics.} Under the slot-module hypothesis (Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}: the composite space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, a graded $U(2)$ slot module tensored with one pair system, with hypercharge from the centre of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, the slot module generated from a unique vacuum by one doublet of slot creation operators, the chirality a CPT halving that is the grading of the joint Clifford system once the slots are fermionic, and slot and pair operators one Clifford system):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Odd slots.)} If the slot quanta are tower elements of one tower parity $\pi$ whose tower grading $(-1)^{\pi n + k}$ is the chirality, then $\pi = 1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Slot content.)} $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2}$ as a graded $U(2)$-module, so the composite's state space is the Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W = \Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus W)$ of five modes, two slot modes and three pair modes, a state being a set of occupied slots and occupied pairs, on which $(A, B) \in U(2) \times U(3)$ acts as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$; its particle half is $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Chirality.)} As in Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves} for the three-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}W$, the chirality of a state is the parity of its total mode number.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Exclusion statistics.)} Every $U(2)$-equivariant slot creation map $a^{\dagger} : \C^{2} \otimes F_{n} \to F_{n+1}$ satisfies $a^{\dagger}(u)a^{\dagger}(u') = -a^{\dagger}(u')a^{\dagger}(u)$ for all $u, u' \in \C^{2}$; in particular $a^{\dagger}(u)^{2} = 0$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(One Clifford system.)} The slots are fermionic modes on the same footing as the pairs: the two slot modes and the three pair modes satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations as one system of five modes, so that, by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}, their Majorana combinations generate $\Cl(10)$ acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$, its spinor module, whose parity grading is that module's chirality.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (ii) and (iv) are Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(3) under the premise's generation clause and CPT halving, with no anomaly condition; (v) is the premise's clause (f), applied once (ii) has made the slot module fermionic; (iii) follows from the premise's requirement that the chirality be the grading of the joint Clifford system, which makes it commute with $\Spin(10)$; (i) compares (iii) with a tower grading. The particle half satisfies the four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients}, a consequence here and not a premise.

title: Hypercharge from the global form, pair counting, and consistency
text:
With $Y$ the hypercharge defined before Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}, and with Hypothesis (S) wherever a doublet at the level of one conformal spinor (a twistor-level doublet) enters:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Under (S).) The one-handed listing keeps the states of even total mode number and conjugates the odd ones, or the reverse; the choice is the particle-antiparticle orientation. Write $(j, k)$ for the component of the five-mode state space with $j$ slot modes and $k$ pair modes occupied (mode counts, not the pair of representation dimensions used elsewhere in this paper, for which see the caption of a figure of the original). In the listing that keeps the quark doublet, the component $(1,1)$, as a particle, the lepton doublet is the full conformal spinor, the component $(1,3)$, $Y_{L} = -1/2$, and the empty conformal spinor, the component $(1,0)$, appears only as its conjugate (here both phrases name doublet components of the one-slot listing; the neutrino paper uses ``empty'' and ``filled conformal spinor'' for the grade-zero and grade-three singlets of the single-spinor sector, different objects, Proposition \claimref{neutrino.empty-twistor}). The $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ anomaly coefficient of the two doublets, $3Y_{Q} + Y_{L}$ with the three the colour multiplicity, is then the identity $3 \cdot \tfrac16 - \tfrac12 = 0$; it would equal $1$ if the empty conformal spinor were listed as the particle instead, so the anomaly confirms the orientation the listing fixed. Pair counting fixes $|Y_{L}/Y_{Q}| = 3$; the parity fixes the sign.
\item (Unconditional as a computation on the Fock space of a single conformal spinor, like Proposition \claimref{standard-model.quarks-leptons-two-level-fermion-content}(3).) Listed by the handedness of (1), the sector of a single conformal spinor gives the singlet spectrum. Here $\CS = \Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}W$, the conformal spinor space, and $\CSm{} = \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}W$ are the two chirality halves (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}), and the listing keeping the even grades and conjugating the odd ones gives
\[
(1)_{0} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{-2/3} \;\oplus\; (\bar{3})_{+1/3} \;\oplus\; (1)_{+1},
\]
that is $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$, $e^{c}$ with hypercharges $0, -\tfrac23, +\tfrac13, +1$: the observed singlet spectrum, with the fourth singlet at hypercharge zero. (The listing by the opposite handedness is the conjugate of this one, the same spectrum in the opposite convention.) Under (S) the grade-$k$ states of a single conformal spinor are the $(0, k)$ components, the states with no slot mode and $k$ pair modes occupied (their content $\Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ and weight $-2k$ match, and irreducibles are determined by content and weight), so their parity is the total parity and this listing is the same listing as in (1).
\item (Consistency, and uniqueness given the content; under (S) for the doublets.) With the content of (1) and (2), all four anomaly conditions of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} hold. Conversely, for the field content $Q = (2,3)$, $L = (2,1)$, $u^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $d^{c} = (1,\bar{3})$, $e^{c} = (1,1)$, all listed in one handedness, together with a fourth singlet of hypercharge zero or no fourth singlet, and $Y_{Q} = 1/6$ as the normalisation, the four conditions determine $Y_{L}$, $Y(e^{c})$ and $\{Y(u^{c}), Y(d^{c})\}$ uniquely, and the solution is the spectrum of (1) and (2). Both hypotheses are necessary: with a fourth singlet of unconstrained hypercharge the conditions admit a one-parameter family, and if the doublets were listed in the opposite handedness from the singlets the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$ and cubic sums would be $-\tfrac23$ and $+\tfrac49$ rather than zero.
\end{enumerate}

title: Imported: the Fock representation of a Clifford algebra, and its Bogoliubov group
text: Let $E$ be a complex vector space of dimension $n$ with a Hermitian inner product, and let $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ be the Fock space of $n$ fermionic modes, with creation operators the exterior multiplications and annihilation operators the contractions. The $2n$ Majorana combinations of these operators generate an action of the complex Clifford algebra of a $2n$-dimensional orthogonal space on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$, which is its irreducible spinor module; the parity grading $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}} \oplus \Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}$ is the chirality decomposition into the two half-spinor modules. The orthogonal transformations of the Majorana generators preserve the canonical anticommutation relations and are implemented on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ by the group $\mathrm{Pin}(2n)$, the connected component $SO(2n)$ by $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$, which acts on each half-spinor module irreducibly for $n \ge 2$; the transformations preserving the complex structure of $E$, equivalently the mode number, form $U(n) \subset SO(2n)$, acting on $\Lambda^{\bullet}E$ as $\Lambda^{\bullet}(g)$ up to a determinant phase. For $n = 3$ this is the structure of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-pair-systems-two-chirality-halves}; for $n = 5$ it is $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ with $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Lecture~20, \S 20.1]{FultonHarris1991} for the spinor module as an exterior algebra and its half-spin decomposition; \cite[Ch.~I, \S\S 2, 5]{LawsonMichelsohn1989} for $\mathrm{Spin}(2n)$ as the double cover of $SO(2n)$ and its spin representation; the Fock-space form is the standard second-quantised reading of the same construction.

title: Imported: the frozen point and the dictionary
text:
On the Einstein region with $\Lambda \neq 0$ of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), the frozen point $I$ is the scale tractor parallel for the tractor gauge field of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}, of squared norm $Q(I) = \Lambda/3 = H^{2}$, and in the flat chart of the conformal model (the flat twistor chart, the flat background itself) its frozen point is $I_{\Lambda} = n_{\infty} + (\Lambda/6)\,n_{0}$. Mass is conformal weight read against it: a density of weight $w$ coupled to the frozen point obeys the Klein-Gordon equation with
\[
m^{2} = -\,w(w+3)\,\frac{\Lambda}{3} = \Delta(3-\Delta)\,H^{2}, \qquad \Delta = -w,
\]
so a real weight gives $m^{2} \ge 0$ only on $w \in [-3, 0]$, where $m \le 3H/2$, and every heavier field has complex weight $w = -\tfrac32 \pm i\nu$ with $\nu \approx m/H$. In particular the weight of the Planck mass is complex, and its imaginary part is
\[
N := \operatorname{Im} w(M_{P}) \approx M_{P}/H, \qquad\text{about } 1.0 \times 10^{61}.
\]
Throughout this paper $N$ means $M_{P}/H$, the number the dictionary attaches to the Planck mass. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Thms.~4.5, 4.7]{ButlerT6} for the frozen point and its norm; \cite[Thm.~3.1, Cor.~3.2]{ButlerT11} for the dictionary and the complex weights; \cite[Lem.~5.1]{ButlerT11} for the chart form of $I_{\Lambda}$. The value, about $1.0 \times 10^{61}$ for $G = M_{P}^{-2}$, is the measured ratio $M_{P}/H$ and carries the record's status \cite{PDG2024}.

title: The internal symmetry ladder
text: For a system of $n$ conformal spinors (an $n$-twistor system) $(Z^{1}, \ldots, Z^{n})$, the linear mixings $Z^{i} \mapsto U^{i}{}_{j} Z^{j}$ that preserve the total momentum $p_{AA'} = \sum_{i} \pi^{i}_{A}\bar\pi^{i}_{A'}$, built from the parts $\pi^{i}$ in the $E = +1$ eigenspace, and the total helicity form $\sum_{i} \bar{Z}^{i} \cdot Z^{i}$, the reversion form $h$ summed over the spinors, for every configuration form exactly the unitary group $U(n)$. The ladder therefore reads: one conformal spinor, massless, internal group $U(1)$; two, the first massive step, internal group $U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$; three, internal group $U(3)$, with Lie algebra $\su(3) \oplus \uu(1)$. (The groups are $U(n)$ themselves, not products: the map $SU(n) \times U(1) \to U(n)$, $(a, \mu) \mapsto \mu a$, is onto, and its kernel is $\{(\mu^{-1}I_{n}, \mu) : \mu^{n} = 1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}_{n}$ by the determinant, so $U(n) = (SU(n) \times U(1))/\mathbb{Z}_{n}$; the distinction is treated in the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form''.)

title: The mass bracket is a charged singlet
text:
Under the $U(2)$ of the two-spinor step (two conformal spinors, mixed by their slot index), the mass bracket transforms by the determinant:
\[
\br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}} \mapsto \det(U) \cdot \br{\pi^{1}\pi^{2}}.
\]
It is therefore an $SU(2)$ singlet carrying charge one under the determinant character (charge two under the scalar phase $e^{I_{6}\theta}\,\id$, whose determinant is $e^{2I_{6}\theta}$, with $I_{6}$ the complex unit of $\CS$): its modulus is the mass (Fact \claimref{mass.mass-symplectic-area-two-twistor-formula}), its phase is pure gauge under the $U(1)$, and it vanishes exactly on the massless locus. Under the global form of the section ``The gauge algebra and the global form'', with the hypercharge of the section ``Content, charges, chirality'', the bracket of two conformal spinors, each the vacuum of its pair system, transforms as $(1, 1)$ with abelian weight $6$, hypercharge $Y = +1$: the quantum numbers of $e^{c}$, and not those of a weak doublet. (The bracket is defined on conformal spinors; what it would be for an excited composite depends on the state space, and is not defined here.)

title: The spectrum run
text: The running Proposition \claimref{standard-model.weak-angle-over-derived-generation} deferred is performed here at one loop, in the normalisation and with the matching relations of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-one-loop-running-trace-ratio}(a): $a_{1} = \tfrac35\,\alpha_{Y}^{-1}$, $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}^{-1} = \tfrac53 a_{1} + a_{2}$, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z}) = \alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(M_{Z})/\alpha_{2}(M_{Z}) = \alpha_{\mathrm{em}}\,a_{2}$. The unification condition determines $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z})$ as an exact rational function of the inputs $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}^{-1}(M_{Z})$, $\alpha_{s}^{-1}(M_{Z})$ and the coefficients $b_{i}$. With the Standard Model coefficients $(\tfrac{41}{10}, -\tfrac{19}{6}, -7)$, those of three derived generations and one Higgs doublet, the doublet being imported rather than derived (Observation \claimref{standard-model.places-outside-state-space}(b)), and the inputs $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}^{-1}(M_{Z}) = 128$, $\alpha_{s}(M_{Z}) = 0.118$ (the record's values to this precision \cite{PDG2024}), the prediction is $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z}) = 78761/379488 = 0.2075\ldots$ with $M_{U} \approx 7 \times 10^{14}$ GeV, against the measured $0.2312$, whose record uncertainty is in the fourth decimal place \cite{PDG2024}: a ten-percent miss, about ninety times the spread the prediction inherits from the record's $\alpha_{s} = 0.1180 \pm 0.0009$ alone ($\pm 0.00027$), before two-loop and threshold effects; and the three couplings do not meet at a common scale, the pairwise meetings of $(a_{1}, a_{2})$, $(a_{1}, a_{3})$ and $(a_{2}, a_{3})$ falling at three different values of $L = \ln(M_{U}/M_{Z})$. So the natural conjecture, the desert (that the derived content, with the one imported doublet, alone connects the structural scale to experiment), is false, whatever the number of generations, complete multiplets being inert, and without the doublet the miss is larger, $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z}) = 3457/16992 = 0.2034$: as the precision era established for minimal unification generally \cite{Amaldi1991}, and as the framework, deriving the content, inherits. The refutation has a quantitative form: with partner-type intermediate content, the supersymmetric coefficients $(\tfrac{33}{5}, 1, -3)$ being the known working example, the same exact function returns $\sin^{2}\theta_{W}(M_{Z}) = 6539/28320 = 0.23089\ldots$ with $M_{U} \approx 2 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, the three pairwise meetings at the record falling at $2.0$, $2.2$ and $2.3 \times 10^{16}$ GeV, within about fifteen percent of one another in scale: agreement at the $10^{-3}$ level. The framework's $3/8$ therefore survives experiment only if the running between the weak and structural scales differs from that of the derived content: either the spectrum between the scales carries partner-like content, which this paper does not derive, or the gauge symmetry is enlarged at an intermediate scale, which the section ``An intermediate symmetry: the slot/pair split'' derives from the split between slots and pairs under Hypothesis (S); whether the framework's own pair and tower structure, every mode already paired and eight towers derived \cite{ButlerT3, ButlerT14}, supplies it is the running programme's question, stated here as its first exact target and flagged at observation level. The closed-form arithmetic is proved; the running, the coefficients and the measured values are Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-one-loop-running-trace-ratio}(a)'s, at assembly and record level.

title: Under (S): the composite's state space is the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ spinor, and the derived generation is its even half
text:
Assume Hypothesis (S). Let $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ act on $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$ through $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$, so that on the component $\Lambda^{j}\C^{2} \otimes \Lambda^{k}\C^{3}$ the abelian factor $\lambda$ acts by $\lambda^{3j - 2k}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The one-generation spectrum of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.hypercharge-global-form-pair-counting-consistency},
\[
Q \oplus L \oplus u^{c} \oplus d^{c} \oplus e^{c} \oplus \nu^{c}
\;=\; (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{-2/3} \oplus (1,\bar{3})_{1/3} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,1)_{0},
\]
is exactly the even part $\Lambda^{\mathrm{even}}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$, sixteen-dimensional, with $\nu^{c}$, $u^{c}$, $Q$, $L$, $e^{c}$, $d^{c}$ at $(j, k) = (0,0), (0,2), (1,1), (1,3), (2,0), (2,2)$; and the odd part $\Lambda^{\mathrm{odd}}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3})$ is its dual, the antiparticles, with the doublet of the empty conformal spinor (the empty-twistor doublet) $(2,1)_{1/2}$ at $(1,0)$. The mass bracket's slot factor $\Lambda^{2}\C^{2}$, $(1,1)_{1}$, is the even component $(2,0)$, the same representation as $e^{c}$.
\item The five-mode Fock space $\Lambda^{\bullet}(\C^{2} \oplus \C^{3}) = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ is the spinor module of $\Cl(10)$, its two parities are the two half-spinor representations of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, and the automorphisms of the five-mode state space's canonical anticommutation relations induced by orthogonal maps of its ten Majorana generators form $O(10)$, implemented on the Fock space by $\mathrm{Pin}(10)$, with the connected part $SO(10)$ implemented by $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ (Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}). The derived generation is therefore the half-spinor $16$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ restricted to $S(U(2) \times U(3))$, with the slots of the conformal spinors as two of the five modes and the pairs as the other three; the automorphisms preserving in addition the mode number form $U(5)$, and those preserving the slot-pair split as well form $U(2) \times U(3)$, of which Theorem \claimref{standard-model.global-form-quotient-determined}'s group is the determinant-one part. (The number-preserving subgroup of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ is a double cover of $U(5)$ acting as $\Lambda^{\bullet} \otimes \det^{-1/2}$, the "determinant phase" of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov}; the action $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ declared above is that of $U(2) \times U(3) \subset SO(10)$, and the two agree on the determinant-one subgroup, where every hypercharge of this paper is computed.)
\item Among the abelian generators of the split-and-number-preserving algebra, acting on the component $(j,k)$ by $\alpha j + \beta k$ with $\alpha, \beta$ real (hypercharge being $(\alpha, \beta) = (\tfrac12, -\tfrac13)$, the pair $(3,-2)$ divided by six):
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] in the action $\Lambda^{\bullet}(A \oplus B)$ declared above, the $[SU(3)]^{2}U(1)$, $[SU(2)]^{2}U(1)$ and gravitational sums of Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-anomaly-coefficients} over the derived generation are $2(2\alpha + 3\beta)$, $2(2\alpha + 3\beta)$ and $8(2\alpha + 3\beta)$, and the cubic sum is a cubic form in $(\alpha, \beta)$ vanishing at $(3,-2)$; so the three linear conditions hold if and only if the generator is a multiple of hypercharge, the total mode number $j + k$ having sums $(10, 10, 40, 400)$ and $j - k$ having $(-2, -2, -8, -32)$;
\item[(b)] in the action the state space carries, that of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ through $\Lambda^{\bullet} \otimes \det^{-1/2}$ in (2), the generator acts by $\alpha j + \beta k - \tfrac12(2\alpha + 3\beta)$, and all four sums, together with the mixed sums $Y^{2}X$ and $YX^{2}$ with hypercharge, vanish for every $(\alpha, \beta)$.
\end{enumerate}
The thirteenth generator of the five-mode state space's automorphism algebra is therefore anomaly-free in the action the generation carries. It is
\[
X \;=\; j + k - \tfrac52 \;=\; 2Y - \tfrac52\,(B - L), \qquad B - L \;:=\; 1 - \tfrac23\,k,
\]
the pair-number form of the operator $B - L$ of Fact \claimref{families.doublet-direction-module-georgi-jarlskog-clebsch}, and it takes the values $-\tfrac52$ on $\nu^{c}$, $-\tfrac12$ on $Q$, $u^{c}$, $e^{c}$ and $\tfrac32$ on $L$, $d^{c}$: the $U(1)_{X}$ of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$. The automorphism rule of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}, read with anomaly cancellation, returns thirteen generators. The thirteenth is broken by the right-handed neutrino's Majorana bilinear $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$, which carries $X = -5$ and $B - L = 2$ (Proposition \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}), and the twelve are what survives below that scale.
\end{enumerate}
Without (S) the first statement is a theorem about a spectrum and an exterior algebra that happen to coincide, with the exterior algebra an object the paper never built; the second is Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-fock-representation-clifford-algebra-bogoliubov} instantiated and is not available; the third is a computation on the table of components and is not needed.

title: Commuting copies
text:
Inside $T_k$, let $B_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the $2k$ plane generators $e_1, f_1, \dots, e_k, f_k$, and let $A_k$ be the subalgebra generated by the twisted base generators $x^{(k)} := x\,\omega_1 \omega_2 \cdots \omega_k$ for $x$ among the ground generators. Then: $B_k \cong \Cl(k,k) \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$; $A_k \cong \Cl(p,q)$ via $x \mapsto x^{(k)}$ (the twisted generators satisfy the ground Clifford relations); $A_k$ and $B_k$ commute elementwise; and multiplication $A_k \otimes B_k \to T_k$ is an isomorphism of algebras,
\[
\Cl(p{+}k, q{+}k) \;\cong\; \Cl(p,q) \otimes \Mat_{2^k}(\R) \;=\; \Mat_{2^k}(\Cl(p,q)).
\]
The isomorphism is canonical given the ordered planes, and compatible with the tower embeddings up to the twist tracked in the section ``The CAR limit''.

title: Fock module; one qubit per rung
text: Let $W_k := \operatorname{span}\{v_1, \dots, v_k\}$, a maximal isotropic subspace of $H_1 \perp \cdots \perp H_k$. The Chevalley action ($v_j$ by wedge, $w_j$ by contraction against the pairing) makes the exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet W_k$, of dimension $2^k$, an irreducible module over $B_k \cong \Mat_{2^k}(\R)$, with the vacuum $1 \in \Lambda^0$ annihilated by every $w_j$ and cyclic for the $v_j$. Each rung doubles the module: $\Lambda^\bullet W_{k+1} = \Lambda^\bullet W_k \otimes \Lambda^\bullet \R v_{k+1}$, one qubit per rung.

title: The ladder pairs satisfy the CAR, as vectors
text:
In $T_k$, the adjoined null pairs satisfy, exactly and at the level of vectors,
\[
v_i v_j + v_j v_i = 0, \qquad w_i w_j + w_j w_i = 0, \qquad v_i w_j + w_j v_i = \delta_{ij}\,,
\]
for all $1 \leq i, j \leq k$: a system of $k$ fermionic modes, with no normal-ordering, no completion, and no representation chosen. Adding a rung adds one mode and touches none of the existing relations.

title: The *-structure of the tower, and its C*-norms
text: Fix the tower's frames: an orthogonal ground frame $x_1, \dots, x_n$ diagonalising $Q$, and the plane frames $e_j, f_j$. On each complexified floor $T_k^{\,\C}$ there is a unique conjugate-linear antiautomorphism $*$ with $x^* = x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = 1$ and $x^* = -x$ for every frame generator with $x^2 = -1$. Under it: every frame generator, every blade in the frame, and every ground or plane volume element is unitary ($z^* z = 1$); the ladder pairs are mutually adjoint, $v_j^* = w_j$; the connecting maps $\iota_k$, the identifications $\varphi_k$ of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, the block doublings $\theta_k$, and the correctors $V_k$ and $W_k$ of Lemma \claimref{tower.compatibility-connecting-maps-transported} and Theorem \claimref{tower.algebraic-limit-even-charge} are all compatible with $*$ (the maps are *-homomorphisms, the correctors unitary). If moreover $p - q$ is even, each $T_k^{\,\C}$ is *-isomorphic to $\Mat_{2^{m/2}}(\C)$, $m := n + 2k$, with $*$ the conjugate transpose; consequently each floor carries a unique C*-norm, every unital *-monomorphism between floors is isometric, and the increasing union $\bigcup_k T_k^{\,\C}$ carries a unique C*-norm.

title: Witt index is quantum capacity
text: For any nondegenerate real quadratic space $(V, Q)$, the maximal number of pairwise-anticommuting fermionic mode pairs realisable by \emph{vectors} of $\Cl(V, Q)$ (families $(a_i, b_i)$ of vectors satisfying the displayed CAR of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) is exactly the Witt index $\min(p,q)$ of $Q$. Along the tower the Witt index is $\min(p,q) + k$: each rung raises the algebra's mode capacity by exactly one, and by no more.

title: Minimality
text:
Let $(\mathbb{W}, f)$ be any null-lift completion of $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$. Then $\mathbb{W}$ contains at least one direction of positive square and one of negative square; in particular $\dim \mathbb{W} \geq 2$, and enlargements of signature increment $(+k, 0)$ or $(0, +k)$ are excluded for every $k$. A single hyperbolic plane suffices, and any two-dimensional $\mathbb{W}$ admitted by the definition is a hyperbolic plane; hence the minimal completion is
\[
\Cl(p,q) \;\longrightarrow\; \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1),
\]
with the adjoined space unique up to isometry, and the signature increment is $(+1,+1)$ in every signature.

title: No-go at the level of elements
text: Let $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$ be nondegenerate of mixed signature $(p,q)$, $p, q \geq 1$, with $n = p + q \geq 3$, and let $\Ncone \subset \mathbb{V}$ be its null cone. Let $(\mathbb{V}', Q')$ be \emph{any} extension of $(\mathbb{V}, Q)$ in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.transport.extension-quadratic-spaces}, possibly $\mathbb{V}$ itself. Then there is no map $\sigma : \Ncone \to \Cl(\mathbb{V}')$ satisfying $v\,\sigma(v)\,v = v$ for every null $v$ that is equivariant, in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.transport.equivariance}, even under the identity component $\Spin^0(p,q)$; a fortiori none equivariant under $\Spin(p,q)$ or $\Pin(p,q)$. Equivariant division by zero is impossible at the level of elements, in the Clifford algebra of every ascent, however large.
